# VelociBar

> VelociBar is a macOS menu bar app that continuously measures your real internet speed over time, instead of only at the moment you run a one-off test. It runs discreet background download/latency tests, keeps a local history, and exports it to CSV so you can prove ISP throttling or slowdowns. Site: https://velocibar.app

VelociBar is built for people who pay for a fast plan but feel their connection is slow. Traditional speed tests (Speedtest, Fast.com) measure under ideal conditions and can show a best-case snapshot; some ISPs even prioritize traffic when they detect a speed-test site is open. VelociBar instead samples your connection minute by minute in the background to reveal what you actually get while working, gaming, or on video calls.

## Key facts

- Platform: macOS 26.0 or later (menu bar / status bar app).
- What it measures: real download throughput (Mbps) and responsiveness under load (RPM, a bufferbloat indicator), rated Low/Medium/High. It alternates two engines: Apple's built-in networkQuality tool and a real download from a global CDN.
- Schedule: automatic background tests every 15, 30 or 60 minutes (your choice), plus an on-demand "Run now" and a desktop widget.
- History: all results are stored locally on your Mac and can be exported as a CSV (timestamp, source/engine, download_mbps, latency_ms, responsiveness_rpm).
- Privacy: no accounts, no cloud, no tracking, no telemetry. Data never leaves your Mac unless you export it yourself.
- Pricing: paid app ($1.99 USD on the US App Store, one-time purchase; local pricing varies by country).
- Languages: Spanish (default) and English.
- Download: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/velocibar/id6756196355

## What makes it different

- Continuous monitoring vs. one-off tests: it records the full picture of your connection, not a single best moment.
- Throttling detection: spots systematic speed drops at specific times of day (for example evening peak-hour congestion) that a point-in-time test would miss.
- Exportable evidence: produces an objective CSV log you can send to your ISP's technical support instead of saying "it feels slow."
- Lightweight and unobtrusive: lives in the menu bar, uses few resources, and can pause tests on battery or weak signal.

## Common questions

- Does it replace Speedtest or Fast.com? No — those remain useful for spot checks. VelociBar adds historical context, automatic alerts, and exportable evidence to complement them.
- Does it upload my data? No. Results are stored only on your Mac.
- Can I export results for my ISP? Yes — full history as a CSV (date, time, download_mbps, latency_ms).
- Does it run in the background? Yes — it runs scheduled tests from the menu bar while you work.
- How much load does it add? Tests are calibrated not to saturate your bandwidth; you set the frequency and it pauses on battery or weak signal.
